full_caption: Nikolai Grimsby-Hale, Appellant, v. Blackthorn Ridge Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellee
court: Marrowdale Land and Property Court, Windmere Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Appellant Nikolai Grimsby-Hale is the record owner of the residential building located at 44 Mill Race Way, Windmere, MD, a 18-unit structure operated as rental housing since 1991. Appellee Blackthorn Ridge Capital Servicing, LLC occupied Unit 1A under a written lease dated September 25, 2022.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The security deposit of $3,500 was not returned within 30 days of surrender, nor was an itemized statement of deductions furnished. The statutory consequence is forfeiture of the landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The record establishes that Nikolai Grimsby-Hale received written notice of the heating defect on July 6, 2014 and did not dispatch a repair contractor until June 1, 2019, an interval of 30 days. During that interval overnight interior temperatures fell below fifty-five degrees on at least eleven occasions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The lease provided for monthly rent of $2,400, due on the first day of each month, with a late charge of $125 assessed on any installment remaining unpaid after the 15th day of the month. The trial court found that this charge operated as a penalty rather than as liquidated damages.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: A late fee is enforceable only where it bears a reasonable relationship to the administrative cost actually incurred by the landlord in processing a delinquent payment. A charge of $125 against a monthly obligation of $2,400 exceeds that relationship and is unenforceable to the extent it exceeds five percent of the installment.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Retaliatory eviction is presumed where a landlord commences a summary possession action within 18 months after a tenant has reported a code violation to the municipal housing inspector. The presumption is rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence of an independent, non-retaliatory ground.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A tenant electing to withhold rent under the repair-and-deduct statute must (1) give written notice of the defect, (2) allow a reasonable time for cure, and (3) deposit the withheld sums with the clerk of court or into a segregated account. Blackthorn Ridge Capital Servicing, LLC satisfied the first two requirements but did not deposit the withheld rent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Nikolai Grimsby-Hale served a notice to quit on August 28, 2020. The notice recited the ground of non-payment but omitted the amount claimed to be due. A notice to quit that fails to state the sum demanded does not commence the statutory cure period.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The trial court awarded Blackthorn Ridge Capital Servicing, LLC attorney's fees of $9,000 under the reciprocal-fee provision. Where a lease grants fees to the landlord, this State reads the provision as mutual, and the prevailing tenant recovers on the same terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Blackthorn Ridge Capital Servicing, LLC withheld rent for the months of February and July of 1996, asserting that the premises were untenantable by reason of a persistent failure of the heating system and recurring water intrusion at the north wall of the unit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: We affirm in part and reverse in part. The judgment of possession is vacated; the money judgment is remanded for recalculation consistent with the late-fee holding set out above.

sections.heading: RIDER F — UTILITY ALLOCATION
sections.text: Where utilities are master-metered, Landlord shall allocate charges among units by the ratio of occupied square footage and shall furnish, upon written request, a copy of the master bill and the allocation calculation for any billing period within the preceding twelve months. Landlord shall not impose an administrative markup exceeding 15 percent of the actual charge.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.
